context: Yumiko explains an old harvest moon viewing tradition to Sho-young.
purpose: Grandmother teaching child cultural moon ritual.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.en: Do you know about moon viewing?
lines.style: Warm, patient opening. Soft voice inviting a child to listen. Slight pause before the question—giving him space to think. The tone of someone sharing something she loves.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.style: Quiet wonder. Small voice, genuine awe, not performed. Eyes up. The observation of a child noticing something true and saying it simply, without self-consciousness.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: 昔から、団子、お供えするの。
lines.en: A long time ago, people would offer dango to the moon.
lines.style: Leisurely teaching voice. Warm, unhurried. Settling into a story she knows well and wants him to know. Soft consonants, no rush.

lines.speaker: sho_child
lines.en: They look delicious—I want to eat one!
lines.style: Bright child-eager. Quick, genuine excitement. No performance, just honest hunger and delight. Small laugh underneath. Immediate and unguarded.

lines.speaker: yumiko_mom
lines.jp: ふふ、一緒に、いただきましょう。
lines.style: Soft, fond laugh on the opening breath. Warm permission wrapped in companionship. Voice settling into contentment. The words of someone delighted to say yes to a child's wish.
